title: Lobster and Clam Bake
description: Quite simply, this is the indoor version of a clambake (without the hot rocks and seaweed). If you can't gain access to a beach and are craving a simple, but special treat, this lobster boil can evoke memories of evening by the ocean in a downtown apartment. The secret to getting everything to cook at the same time is to layer the seafood on top of the potato, corn and sausage. This version uses kielbasa, but a chorizo or even andouille could be a delicious addition to this recipe.
ingredients: 1 pkg (13 oz) Polish Kielbasa, cut in 8 pieces on bias
4 ears corn, shucked, cut in half
directions: Rinse clams and mussels well under cold running water; discard any that are broken or open.
Add water, potatoes, and kielbasa to steamer base; cover. Bring to boil on HIGH; reduce heat to MED.

Layer clams, lobsters, corn, and mussels in steamer insert; add to base. Cover; steam about 15-20 min, until lobster reaches 145 degrees (check by inserting thermometer halfway into thickest part of lobster).
Remove steamer insert; discard any unopened clams and mussels. Transfer contents onto parchment paper-covered table or extra-large platter.

Strain potatoes and kielbasa from base; reserve broth. Add potatoes and kielbasa to seafood mix; garnish with lemon wedges. Strain broth into bowl; serve immediately with seafood – and, of course, plenty of melted butter
